Goods Movement
 
1. RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVE REQUEST FOR 2026-2029 ON-CALL MULTIMODAL PLANNING CONSULTING SERVICES AGREEMENTS WITH: DB E.C.O. NORTH AMERICA INC., HATCH ASSOCIATES CONSULTANTS, INC., ITERIS INC., LOGSUM LLC, MOFFATT & NICHOL, AND WSP USA INC.
 
Summary: Staff requests approval of on-call professional services agreements for a term of three years each, for the cumulative amount of $1,397,000, between the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) and the following six firms: DB E.C.O. North America Inc.(DB), Hatch Associates Consultants, Inc. (Hatch), Iteris, Inc. (Iteris), LogSum LLC (LogSum), Moffatt & Nichol (M&N), and WSP USA Inc. (WSP). The Goods Movement Division (GMD) requires outside professional services for a variety of purposes including, but not limited to, the following: grant applications; traffic studies, and terminal/rail system simulation and capacity analyses. These services pertain to, and aid in implementing Objective 1 (World Class Infrastructure that Promotes Growth) of the “Port of Los Angeles 2026-2030 Strategic Plan,” and specifically Initiatives 1 and 3. The Harbor Department will be financially responsible for payment of expenses incurred under the proposed agreements.
 
Recommendation: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) find that in accordance with the Los Angeles City Charter Section 1022, work under the subject agreements can be performed more feasibly by outside consultants than by City employees; 3) approve and award six on-call professional services agreements for a term of three years each to the following firms (and not-to-exceed amounts): DB ($237,000), Hatch ($251,000), Iteris ($224,000), LogSum ($237,000), M&N ($224,000) and WSP ($224,000); 4) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to said agreements, for and on behalf of the Board; and 5) adopt Resolution No. __________.

Information Technology
 
2. RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - FIRST AMENDMENTS TO AGREEMENTS BETWEEN THE CITY OF LOS ANGELES HARBOR DEPARTMENT AND BIRDI SYSTEMS, INC., BURNS ENGINEERING, INC., INFOJINI INC., SATWIC INC., AND SIERRA CYBER, LLC, FOR ON-CALL/AS-NEEDED INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
 
Summary: Staff requests approval of the First Amendments (Amendments) to Agreement Nos. 24-10046 with Birdi Systems, Inc. (Birdi), 24-10047 with Burns Engineering, Inc. (Burns), 24-10048 with Infojini Inc. (Infojini), 24-10049 with Satwic Inc. (Satwic), and 24-10050 with Sierra Cyber, LLC (Sierra Cyber) (Agreements). Due to the various projects supported, these Agreements align with more than one Strategic Plan Objective. The objectives are Objective 2: An Efficient, Secure, and Sustainable Supply Chain, and Objective 3: Improved Financial Performance of Port Assets. The scope of the Agreements is for information technology services on an on-call, as-needed basis. The term of the Agreements is for three years commencing on September 18, 2024, and expiring on September 17, 2027. The current not-to-exceed amount for all Agreements is a collective pool of $6,000,000. The proposed amendments will increase the collective not-to-exceed amount pool by $3,000,000 to $9,000,000. This increase is necessary due to consolidation of technology consulting contracts, the additional technical resources needed for capital and operating projects, and other essential IT support services. Payment of expenditures incurred under the Agreements will continue to be the financial responsibility of the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department).
 
Recommendation: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) find that in accordance with the Los Angeles City Charter Section 1022, the services required can be performed more feasibly by outside contractors than by City employees; 3) approve the proposed First Amendments to the Agreements with Birdi Systems, Inc., Burns Engineering, Inc., Infojini Inc., Satwic Inc., and Sierra Cyber, LLC, increasing the collective not-to-exceed amounts from $6,000,000 to $9,000,000; 4) authorize the Executive Director to execute and the Board Secretary to attest to said Amendments for and on behalf of the Board; and 5) adopt Resolution No. _____________

3. RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVAL OF ORDERS DIRECTING SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA GAS COMPANY AND PBF ENERGY WESTERN REGION LLC TO RELOCATE OR REMOVE PIPELINES AND CONDUITS INTERFERING WITH THE 22ND STREET PARKING LOT PROJECT AND HARBOR BLVD AND 22ND STREET ROADWAY PROJECT
 
Summary: Staff requests approval of the Orders directing City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department) tenants Southern California Gas Company (So Cal Gas) and PBF Energy Western Region LLC (PBF), to relocate or remove pipelines that are interfering with the 22nd Street Parking Lot Project and Harbor Boulevard and 22nd Street Roadway Project (Projects). These proposed Orders will serve as a notice to the impacted Harbor Department tenants that they must promptly remove their abandoned pipelines, in accordance with their agreements with the Harbor Department. All costs associated with the removal of affected pipelines are the financial responsibility of the respective tenants.
 
Recommendation: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed actions is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) approve the Order directing Southern California Gas Company to relocate or remove its pipelines pursuant to Section 9(h) of Order No. 4506; 3) approve the Order directing PBF Energy Western Region LLC to relocate or remove its pipelines pursuant to Section 106.4 of Permit No. 936; 4) authorize the Board Secretary to attest to the Orders directing the aforementioned Harbor Department tenants to relocate or remove their pipelines; and 5) Adopt Resolution No. __________________; and Order Nos. ____________________________.

Regular Item No. 4
 
Debt & Financial Analysis
 
4. RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVING THE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY OF CERTAIN DOCUMENTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE ISSUANCE BY THE ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY OF ONE OR MORE SERIES OF ITS ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY SUBORDINATE LIEN REVENUE REFUNDING BONDS AND SECOND SUBORDINATE LIEN REVENUE REFUNDING BONDS AND AUTHORIZING SUCH OTHER ACTIONS AS ARE NECESSARY TO ASSIST THE AUTHORITY IN THE ISSUANCE OF SUCH REFUNDING BONDS AND MAKING A DETERMINATION RELATING HERETO
 
Summary: Staff requests approval of certain documents related to the proposed issuance of the Alameda Corridor Transportation Authority (ACTA) Subordinate Lien Revenue Refunding Bonds and Second Subordinate Lien Revenue Refunding Bonds (2026 ACTA Bonds) including certain disclosures required from the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department). The proposed action is aligned with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 3: Improved Performance of Port Assets. Given the Harbor Department’s role as a partial guarantor of ACTA’s debt along with the Port of Long Beach, it must provide certain financial and operating disclosures to the bond market for any ACTA bond transactions, both at the time of the initial offering and for as long as the bonds remain outstanding. ACTA is projecting that its existing cash reserves and future revenues will be insufficient to cover debt service payments over a 13-year period from Fiscal Year (FY) 2028 through FY 2040, and that Shortfall Advances would be required from the two ports to offset the difference. Currently, ACTA projects that the Harbor Department would be responsible for approximately $22.4 million in average annual Shortfall Advances over this 13-year period. Under the proposed transaction, the two ports’ annual average Shortfall Advances would be reduced by extending the duration over which Shortfall Advances are made. Under the proposed transaction, ACTA projects that the Harbor Department would be responsible for approximately $17.7 million in average annual Shortfall Advances over a 17-year period from FY 2028 through FY 2044. Bond market conditions at the time of the transaction and ACTA’s future revenues will determine the level of Shortfall Advance savings that will ultimately be achieved.
 
Recommendation: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) authorize the execution and delivery of the Continuing Disclosure Certificate, the Letter of Representation, and other related documents and certificates in connection with the issuance and sale of the 2026 ACTA Bonds; 3) authorize the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department’s Executive Director or Chief Financial Officer, each of them acting individually, to comply with the terms and intent of the Board’s Resolution, to assist ACTA in the issuance of the 2026 ACTA Bonds, to execute and deliver any documents or instruments related thereto and to take such other actions as may be deemed necessary or desirable in order to carry out the purposes of the Board’s Resolution subject to: (i) approval of the issuance of the 2026 ACTA Bonds by ACTA, and (ii) the conditions set forth in the Resolution; 4) approve certain disclosures relating to the finances and operations of the Harbor Department to be contained in the Preliminary Official Statement and the Official Statement for the 2026 ACTA Bonds including the Audited Financial Statements of the Harbor Department, with such changes thereto as the Executive Director or the Chief Financial Officer may require or approve; and 5) adopt Resolution No. __________.
